menu_options.player: A player with CamAlert: Enigma2 receiver, Kodi or Android TV / Fire TV
menu_options.app: A TV with a notification app (PiPup, TvOverlay or Notifications for Android TV / Fire TV)

player.title: Add a CamAlert player
player.description: A player is an Enigma2 receiver, Kodi or an Android TV / Fire TV device with CamAlert. Port, HTTPS and token as set in CamAlert on the player.

data_description.host: Address of the player (Enigma2 receiver, Kodi or Android TV / Fire TV) with CamAlert, e.g. 192.168.1.10.
data_description.port: Port of the CamAlert API, as set in CamAlert on the player. Default: 8099.
data_description.https: Turn on if HTTPS is on for the API in CamAlert on the player.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off for the player's own (self-signed) certificate. Only used with HTTPS.
data_description.token: Only if an access token is set in CamAlert on the player. It is sent in a header, never in the address.

app.title: Add a TV with a notification app
app.description: No CamAlert on the TV: Home Assistant sends the camera picture to a notification app that already runs on it. Fewer features than a CamAlert player: no mosaic, tour, camera control or colour keys.

data_description.app: PiPup or TvOverlay on the TV, or Home Assistant's own Notifications for Android TV / Fire TV integration.
data_description.name: Optional: the name of the player in Home Assistant.
data_description.host: PiPup and TvOverlay: the address of the TV, e.g. 192.168.1.30.
data_description.notify_entity: Notifications for Android TV / Fire TV: its notify entity. A picture appears when Home Assistant has a camera entity with the camera's name (camera.front_door); otherwise text only.
data_description.go2rtc: The TV fetches pictures and live video straight from this go2rtc, so it must be in your local network, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:1984.
data_description.camera: Optional: the go2rtc name of the camera to show when a request names none, e.g. front_door. Empty: the first camera.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Add {name}
zeroconf_confirm.description: CamAlert found {name} on the network ({host}). Add this player to Home Assistant?

data_description.token: The player has an access token: enter the token set in CamAlert on the player. It is sent in a header, never in the address.

browser_confirm.title: Add {name}
browser_confirm.description: {name} connected to Home Assistant as a CamAlert player: a web page or the browser extension in a browser. Add this player to Home Assistant?

setup.title: Set up {name}
setup.description: {name} has not been set up yet. Home Assistant can send it the address of go2rtc, so the player can show your cameras straight away. Leave the address empty to skip; you can also do this later in the options of the player.

data_description.go2rtc_server: Address of your go2rtc server, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:1984. Filled in when Home Assistant knows a go2rtc it can reach.
data_description.camera: Optional: the go2rtc name of the camera the player shows when no camera is given, e.g. front_door.

error.forbidden: The player refused the request: check the token, or 'Allowed callers' in CamAlert.
error.certificate: The player's certificate is not trusted. For CamAlert's own certificate, turn off Check certificates.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Details are in the Home Assistant log.

abort.wrong_player: This address belongs to another player. Add it as a new player instead.
abort.not_camalert: This device did not say which CamAlert player it is.
abort.browser_player: This player is a web browser: it has no address. Change its settings on the player page in the browser.

init.title: CamAlert player options
init.description: The player is shown in Home Assistant under the device of the TV or Enigma2 receiver it runs on.

data_description.parent_device: Automatic: the device of the Enigma2, Kodi or Android TV integration with the same address as the player. Or choose a device yourself, or none.
data_description.go2rtc_server: Optional: sends this go2rtc address to the player. A player that is already set up only accepts an address in your local network. Empty: the player keeps its own setting.
data_description.camera: Optional, with the go2rtc address: the go2rtc name of the default camera, e.g. front_door.
data_description.doorbell: Optional: when one of these rings (a doorbell event, or a binary sensor that turns on), the player shows the camera with priority high. No automation needed; blueprints remain for your own rules.
data_description.doorbell_camera: The go2rtc name of the camera to show for the doorbell, e.g. front_door. Empty: the player's default camera.
data_description.active_from: Notification app only: requests with priority normal are shown only between these times. Empty: all day. High and alarm always come through.
data_description.active_until: End of the active hours; may be after midnight, e.g. 07:00 to 23:00 or 22:00 to 06:00.

error.invalid_server: This is not a valid address. Use e.g. http://192.168.1.10:1984.
error.already_set_up: The player is already set up and only accepts a go2rtc address in your local network.
error.invalid_camera: Invalid camera name: one go2rtc name, e.g. front_door.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the player. Is it on, is CamAlert installed and is the port correct?
error.forbidden: The player refused the request: check the token, or 'Allowed callers' in CamAlert.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Details are in the Home Assistant log.

options.nfandroidtv: Notifications for Android TV / Fire TV

show.name: Show camera
show.description: Shows one or more cameras on the TV of one or more players. Without a target: every player.

camera.name: Cameras
camera.description: One or more camera names as in go2rtc, e.g. front_door. 2-4 cameras are shown together in the multi-camera window. Empty = default camera of the player.

seconds.name: Duration
seconds.description: How long the camera stays on screen. Empty = setting of the player, 0 = until Hide camera (at most 10 minutes).

mode.name: Display mode
mode.description: Photo window, live view, notification, or the multi-camera window (2-4 cameras, the TV stays visible). Empty = setting of the player.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: Normal follows the rules of the player (do not disturb, time window, not while playing). High always comes through (doorbell). Alarm always comes through and also wakes an Enigma2 receiver from standby.

label.name: Who/what
label.description: Optional text before the camera name in the title, e.g. Person.

announce.name: Spoken announcement
announce.description: Text the players speak with the camera, e.g. "Someone is at the door". Home Assistant makes the speech with a TTS engine; the player setting Spoken announcement decides for which requests (default: doorbell and alarm).

tts.name: TTS engine
tts.description: The text-to-speech engine for the announcement. Empty = the first TTS engine of Home Assistant.

language.name: Language
language.description: Language of the announcement, e.g. en or nl. Empty = the engine's default.

mosaic.name: Show mosaic
mosaic.description: Shows several cameras at once in a full-screen mosaic.

cameras.name: Cameras
cameras.description: Up to 9 camera names. Empty = mosaic setting of the player.

seconds.name: Duration
seconds.description: How long the mosaic stays on screen. Empty = setting of the player.

hide.name: Hide camera
hide.description: Closes the camera window and returns to TV.

ptz.name: Camera control (PTZ)
ptz.description: Pans, tilts or zooms a camera that is listed with ONVIF or Foscam in the devices file of the player.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Name of the camera as in the devices file.

move.name: Movement
move.description: Moves for about half a second, then stops.
